subject: LuminaHealth — VPC packaging, platform fee & SRE retainer (proposal)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: LuminaHealth — VPC packaging, platform fee & SRE retainer (proposal)

Hi Julia — great speaking earlier. Per our call, attaching a compact proposal and a simple pricing grid so procurement has numbers to work with. Two routes that align with what you described (pilot -> production):

1) Pilot Starter (3–5 node median):
- Lower platform fee (monthly) for first 6 months to reduce up-front cost
- Metered GPU usage at standard rate
- Optional SRE retainer: 40 hours/month, reduced SLA (8x5)
- One-time migration credit available for pilot-sized on-prem installs

2) Production Anchor (12+ node commitment):
- Reduced per-token/GPU pricing plus higher platform fee amortized over 12 months
- SRE retainer: 80 hours/month, 24x7 escalation path available as an add-on
- Faster on-call SLAs and guaranteed response SLAs in SOW

Notes / asks for pricing finalization:
- Can you confirm expected peak concurrent GPUs and whether retention for logs is 90/180 days?
- Procurement cadence (PO + net terms) and legal redline ownership for PII addendum

I attached: Lumina_DRAFT_SOW_v2.pdf and LH_pricing_grid_v3.xlsx. If you want, Marissa can run a quick blended TCO showing the amortized platform fee vs metered-only path.

If you want to keep costs low for pilot and still secure a deployment window in Q3, I recommend option 1 with a migration credit and a conversion clause to option 2 at milestone.

Best,

Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0124
From: Julia Park <julia.park@luminahealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@luminahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LuminaHealth — VPC packaging, platform fee & SRE retainer (proposal)

Thanks Dylan — quick follow up from procurement and engineering. A few points: 

- Platform fee: the numbers look reasonable for production, but for pilot we need the platform fee waived for first 60 days (migration credit helps but we can't carry a recurring platform fee during the pilot budget window).
- SRE retainer: our infra team prefers consumption-based SRE hours (pay-for-use) rather than a locked 40 hrs/mo retainer. We can guarantee a minimum of 10 hrs/mo during pilot.
- Migration credit: procurement wants this as a line item on the PO (one-time credit applied to first invoice).
- Legal: net 30 is standard for us; we'd need a PII addendum and SOC2 evidence before signature.

If you can send a counter with those flexes (60-day platform fee waiver, consumption SRE option, credit as PO line item, net30), we can move the PO internally this week.

Julia Park
Head of Product Operations, LuminaHealth
julia.park@luminahealth.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: LuminaHealth — needs: platform fee waiver + consumption SRE — quick recs

Fwding Julia's note — procurement is asking for a 60-day platform fee waiver for the pilot and a consumption-based SRE option (min 10 hrs/mo). They want the migration credit as a PO line item and net30. Can we concede and how far?

My read: Lumina wants low friction for pilot conversion. We can concede a 60-day platform fee waiver if we: 
- Secure a 12-month conversion commitment or
- Take a 15% platform fee discount year-1 if they decline firm commit but agree to conversion milestone metrics (30-day production ramp).

Marissa — can you rework the grid to show both paths? If we do the waiver, offer a one-time migration credit equal to 50% of first-month expected metered usage (capped) and convert SRE retainer to pay-as-you-go with pre-paid blocks (10 / 25 / 50 hr buckets) and rollover for the first 3 months.

Irene — we need SOC2 + PII addendum sign-off path; can we attach the SOC2 package and a redline checklist? Also confirm whether net30 is acceptable in our standard commercial terms or needs exec sign-off for specific accounts.

Proposed internal concession matrix: 
- Waive platform fee for first 60 days for pilot; require PO that lists migration credit as a negative line item.
- Offer SRE as pre-paid buckets (client picks), min 10 hrs/mo during pilot, rollover for 3 months.
- If no 12-mo commit, apply 15% platform fee discount in year 1 until conversion.

If everyone agrees, I'll send an updated quote to Julia today.

Thanks,
Dylan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: LuminaHealth — needs: platform fee waiver + consumption SRE — quick recs

Agree with Dylan's approach. A couple of clarifications and one tweak: 

1) Migration credit: instead of % of first month, propose a fixed migration credit of $12,000 for pilot installations under 6 nodes, $25,000 for 6–15 nodes. Cleaner for PO and easier for bookkeeping.

2) Platform fee waiver: 60 days waiver OK, but include a conversion notice clause: if they don't convert to a paid plan or sign a 12-month conversion within 90 days of pilot end, normal platform fees are back-dated to pilot start (we keep the credit to cover onboarding only). This protects revenue.

3) SRE buckets: offer 10 / 30 / 60 hr pre-paid buckets. For pilot, they pick 10hr pre-paid at discounted hourly rate; unused hours roll over month-to-month for up to 3 months. After production conversion, we re-evaluate bucket sizing.

4) Billing terms: Net30 is standard; if legal redlines the PII addendum, Irene, please flag any need for commercial exec sign-off.

I'll attach a revised pricing grid and a short term-sheet summarizing the concession language. Once Dylan gets the go-ahead, I'll prepare a clean quote with PO-line migration credit and SRE bucket SKUs.

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@luminahealth.com>, procurement <procurement@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: LuminaHealth — VPC packaging, platform fee & SRE retainer (proposal)

Julia — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on internal review we can meet your asks with the following counter (summary below and revised pricing attached):

Counter offer (pilot-friendly):
- Platform fee: waived for first 60 days (pilot). If no conversion to a paid plan or 12-month commitment within 90 days after pilot ends, platform fees will be back-dated to pilot start (we will keep migration credit only).
- Migration credit: one-time line item on PO — fixed credit based on node size: $12,000 (<=5 nodes) or $25,000 (6–15 nodes).
- SRE: consumption buckets (10 / 30 / 60 hrs). Pilot minimum is 10 hrs pre-paid at discounted rate; unused hours roll over up to 3 months.
- Billing: Net 30 ok.
- Compliance: attaching SOC2 snapshot and PII addendum template. Irene (cc) will support legal review.

Next steps we need from you:
1) Confirm planned pilot node count (<=5 or 6–15).
2) Confirm PO timeline (can procurement push a PO with migration credit as line item this week?).
3) Any legal preferences on PII addendum terms to reduce back-and-forth.

I've attached: LH_pricing_grid_v3.xlsx (revised), Lumina_DRAFT_SOW_v2.pdf, SRE_retainer_template.docx. Once you confirm node count and PO timing we will issue a formal quote (with PO-line migration credit) and share a short conversion milestone schedule.

Appreciate the quick collaboration — happy to hop on a 20-min call if that speeds the PO.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
